text: Planning first: the geometry is an annular passage between two surfaces of revolution about the engine (X) axis, 0.9 m long, in **metres** (450/430/410 mm outer, 280/310/250 mm inner → 0.28–0.45 m). I'll build each radius profile as a spline through the three given stations, revolve to solids, subtract inner from outer to get the air volume, tag the four faces, export per-patch STLs, then `blockMesh` + `snappyHexMesh` the annulus. First cell: build the two solids and look at the cut result.

The subtraction worked: two REVOLUTION faces (outer 2.434 m², inner 1.680 m²) and two planar annulus caps. Now I tag the four faces where they're identified (not by bounding box) and export one STL per patch.
`centroid` isn't a method — use `center()` instead; also fix dir creation ordering.
Faces tagged and exported. Now measure the actual radii the spline built at the three stations (compare with the requested 450/430/410 and 280/310/250 mm), then write the OpenFOAM mesh setup.
`Part.section` doesn't exist — I'll measure the radii directly off the exported STL vertices instead (which is what gets meshed anyway).
Binary STL — use pyvista to read it.

Geometry verified to ~1e-4 tolerance (spline hits all specified radii; 0.310 vs 0.31023 at one point is tessellation sampling). Now write the OpenFOAM case: `blockMeshDict` background box and `snappyHexMeshDict` with the four named patches, coarse first.
Missing `controlDict` — add a minimal one, rerun blockMesh, then snappyHexMesh.
`refinementRegions ();` parsed as a bare entry — needs a `dict` body. Fix both empty-dict entries and rerun.
Mesh built: 79,301 cells, all quality checks pass per snappy. Now `checkMesh` and a visual slice.

`checkMesh` says OK: 4 patches, single region, volume 0.2747 m³. Now look at the mesh — slice the domain with pyvista via foamToPython? Can't; use `foamToVTK`? Simpler: render the four STL surfaces plus a mesh slice via `snappy`'s output... Let's just use `foamToVTK` if available.

The picture confirms the annular passage: mesh occupies the gap between coreCowl (inner) and outerCowl, capped by inlet/outlet rings. Last check — compare mesh volume to analytic volume from the STLs.
3% gap — refine the quadrature before trusting it.
Volume converges to 0.2756 m³ against mesh's 0.2747 — within 0.4% (STL tessellation noise). Geometry is consistent and the mesh is clean. Done — summary and declare.
